To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pretreatment HCV RNA levels, genotype and histology are good indicators of response to interferons.

(1) pretreatment HCV RNA level, genotype and liver fibrosis are important predictors of response to IFN-alpha therapy, (2) the patients with low level HCV viremia did respond to IFN-alpha, (3) type 1b HCV was more resistant to IFN-alpha than type 2a.
pretreatment HCV RNA level, genotype, and liver histology were good predictors of response to IFN-alpha therapy in patients with chronic HCV infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of materials, the so-called "magnetic nanoparticles", for use in the field of biomedical applications.
the study of the effects of the interferon-alpha on the liver.
the development of new methods for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of HCV genotype and HCV-RNA titer is an important predictive factor for response to interferon therapy in patients with chronic hepatitis.
HCV genotype, pretreatment viremia and histology are all useful in the selection of patients who are likely to respond to interferon-alpha treatment.
the pretreatment HCV RNA level, the genotype, and liver histology can be used as predictors of the response to IFN therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the response to interferon alpha 2a treatment in chronic hepatitis C virus infected Japanese patients is associated with pretreatment hepatitis C virus genotype, serum hepatitis C virus RNA level and liver histological grade.
the patients with CAHS2a who showed CR--> SR had low HCV-RNA viremia.

the response rate for interferon-alpha 6 MU 3 times a week therapy for 6 months was significantly lower in Japanese patients with genotype 1b than in those with genotype 2a, but the response rates were significantly higher in those with genotype non-1b (1a or 2a) than in those with 1b.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that a combination of interferon and ribavirin therapy is highly effective in the treatment of chronic HCV infection, with sustained response rates of 50% or more in most patients with genotype 1 infection and more than 80% in those with genotype 2 or 3.
genotype 2a is associated with a higher likelihood of a sustained viral response, and that a low level of viremia is associated with a better chance of a complete response.
the HCV-RNA viral load is an independent predictor of response to IFN therapy.
